title: Planning a Newcastle office fit-out budget
excerpt: How to turn a workplace brief, site condition and delivery programme into an estimate you can interrogate and update.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Newcastle Office Fit-Out Budget Planning | YOS
metaDescription: Plan a Newcastle office fit-out budget using the workplace brief, site condition, project scope, assumptions and delivery programme.
body:
## Build the estimate from the project

A useful fit-out budget starts with the actual premises and workplace brief. Generic rates can help test feasibility, but they cannot confirm the price of a project without current scope and market evidence.

## Record the site condition

Document what exists, what can remain and what needs investigation. Include base-building services, approvals, accessibility, fire requirements, power, data, lighting, air conditioning, finishes and any landlord works.

## Define the work packages

Separate design and consultants, approvals, construction, services, technology, furniture, relocation and contingency. State GST treatment and identify anything funded or delivered by the landlord.

## Make assumptions visible

Every estimate should carry a date, source, scope, exclusions, allowances and validity period. Unknown conditions should be labelled rather than hidden inside a confident total.

## Connect cost and programme

Lead times, access constraints, approvals and sequencing affect the delivery plan. Confirm the operational date and work backwards through design, procurement, construction, installation and handover.

## Keep decisions controlled

Record each approved change and its effect on cost, timing and scope. Compare the current forecast with the approved budget throughout delivery.

For a project-specific view, prepare the brief and arrange an evidence-backed estimate for the actual premises. Your Office Space can coordinate that process where the project fits our current capability and delivery area.
